digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate, context-limit escalation and model ladder sizing
propositions: When models_at_or_above is called with a non-Anthropic-family primary model that is not in the ladder, it falls through to return the entire ladder instead of returning the primary itself, causing escalation to downgrade to claude-haiku-4-5 and cross provider families.

When largest_window_tokens is called with a truthy but unlocated primary model, it returns MODEL_LADDER[-1][1] instead of the ladder minimum, overstating the available context window and causing P8 to under-block material that will not fit.

For a non-Anthropic-family primary that context-limits, the prerequisite-coverage escalation path at prerequisites.py:260-261 also jumps to claude-haiku-4-5 via an unlocated rung, crossing providers and downgrades the window via the same falling-through ladder lookup.

The fix changes models_at_or_above to return [model] for a truthy-but-unlocated primary (preserving the one-criterion retry) and largest_window_tokens to return min(w for _, w in MODEL_LADDER) for such a primary, making the unlocated outcome explicit rather than silent.
Three existing test assertions in test_model_class_ladder.py pin the defective behavior and must be updated to reflect the new explicit-outcome contract.

The prerequisites escalation requires no edits to its own source because its existing except (ValueError, IndexError) handler converts the one-element [model] ladder into the input-too-large indeterminate record already emitted at prerequisites.py:263.
